scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false) not the author's working copy. Python CLI/TUI (main.py, src/*.py) read for SQL, file actions and logging. src/old_chomper.py is a legacy copy and tests/ contain many fixtures; hits there were verified or excluded. Test files reference the author's local paths (/home/jcz/Pictures) but are not recorded as findings. Shell scripts (scripts/delete_photos_in_file.sh, tests/filesperdir.sh) are out of scope for full interface/data-access detection in skill version 1.0 and were only skimmed. The 'passwd' sensitive-data hit is a test fixture; latitude/gps hits are real EXIF GPS fields. The .claude/ directory tracks agent prompt and session-note text files (no credentials).

gitignore_gaps: *.pem, *.key and credentials.json are not excluded (*.json and *.conf are excluded generically)

findings: all 15 runtime deps use lower-bound ranges (>=) rather than exact pins; no lockfile committed (*.lock is gitignored)
pyinstaller and altgraph (build tools) are listed as runtime dependencies
python-xmp-toolkit requires the native Exempi library; ffmpeg-python requires the ffmpeg binary

databases.credential_source: none (local files: hash cache, report .db, file-list .db)

sql_injection_risk.reason: all execute calls in src/ use literal SQL with ? placeholders; no string-built SQL found

databases.credential_source: none (report database written alongside CSV/JSON reports)

file_system_access.detail: recursively reads user-specified photo/video directories to hash and extract EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata
deletes (Path.unlink / shutil.rmtree), moves and copies duplicate files; creates backups in photochomper_backups/ and supports rollback
writes CSV/JSON/SQLite duplicate reports and removes a stale report db (os.remove)
deletes files listed in an input text file (has --dry-run and prompt)

sensitive_data_indicators.field_or_variable: camera make/model and file paths in reports

office_and_collaboration_sources.location_or_host: duplicates_report*.csv written to the working directory and read back by --summary

what_this_app_can_do: Scans chosen photo/video folders for exact and similar duplicates using SHA-256 and perceptual hashes (images and videos).
Writes duplicate reports to CSV, JSON and SQLite, including file paths and EXIF metadata such as GPS and camera details.
Can delete, move or copy duplicate files, with backup and rollback, from an interactive TUI.
Keeps a local SQLite hash cache to speed up repeat scans; packages to a Windows exe with PyInstaller.

data_sources_touched.source: User photo and video directories on local disk
Local SQLite hash cache and report databases

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Local command-line/TUI tool run by whoever starts it; no network listener and no login. It acts with that user's file-system permissions.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: Deletes files and directories (shutil.rmtree for directories); mitigated by a backup copy and rollback in src/actions.py
Reports contain GPS coordinates and full local file paths
No network or external data transfer found

top_findings: No secrets, routes or external APIs found
Tool deletes/moves user files (backup and rollback present)
Dependencies use >= ranges with no committed lockfile; build tools listed as runtime deps
